t11.claim: A stale bytecode cache can invert a mutation verdict, so a mutation run must clear it — the guard checks the poisoned IMPORT, not that caches were deleted

The test reproduces the poisoned import with a same-size edit restamped to the old mtime, and carries a CONTROL assertion proving the fixture is genuinely poisoned — that control immediately caught the test un-poisoning itself when it inherited PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE from the runner.

t13.claim: A superseded claim keeps its own derived status and gains a pointer — retiring a finding must not misreport what its evidence actually found

t14.claim: A comparison drawn at one arm's own TRAINING search budget is flagged as home ground; arms measured at different deployment budgets are refused as unpaired
t14.note: L5, found 2026-09-21 by an adversarial audit of h8. The ledger refused mixed provenance, unmatched budgets, drifted code and mislabelled treatments — and never recorded the budget the arms were MEASURED at, so compare() could not notice it equalled exactly one arm's training budget. All 29 entries on disk were drawn at 96 sims: arm A's home value, 3x arm B's. A counter-experiment at 32-sim deployment on identical roots tied 417/512 vs 417/512 (underpowered: its CI contains h8's +0.0342, diff-in-diff z=0.99). t15.claim: A claim must clear the null band ITS OWN registrant declared — a significant effect smaller than that band reads NEGLIGIBLE, not supported
t15.note: Found 2026-09-21 by an adversarial audit of h8. _status filtered on significance FIRST and returned 'supported' before null_below was read, so POWER rather than effect size decided the verdict: a significant +0.029 inside a declared 0.03 band read exactly like a +0.70. Deliberately asymmetric — magnitude gates a claim being ASSERTED, never one being contradicted, since 'a>b' is wrong if b wins significantly however narrowly. Mutation-testing found ALL-vs-ANY untested: a claim with one meaningful replication and one tiny one is SUPPORTED, and only a claim whose every supporting draw is under its own bar is negligible. h8 (+0.0342 vs a 0.03 band) is unaffected and stays supported — by 14%.

t16.claim: A run's cost is summed over EVERY segment and quoted as CPU time; a run whose CPU/wall ratio falls below its thread count is reported as sleep-contaminated, never returned as a clean number
t16.note: Found 2026-09-21: I quoted arm B's cost as 95.8 h three times. t18.claim: One comparison read at several settings is summarised by a POOLED effect with the interaction tested and handed back — reading each setting alone invites the significant/non-significant fallacy
t18.note: §C.34, 2026-09-22. The 96-vs-32 pair was read at three deployment budgets on the SAME 1024 roots: 32 -> +0.0156 (p=0.38, NULL), 64 -> +0.0439 (p=0.0042), 96 -> +0.0342 (p=0.0152). Read one at a time that reads as 'the effect depends on the deployment budget' — which is the significant/non-significant fallacy, and I was one sentence from committing it. The INTERACTION is null (max |z| = 1.30 across all three pairwise diff-in-diffs), so the three are statistically indistinguishable and the honest summary is ONE pooled effect: +0.0312, SE 0.0093, z=3.37, p=0.00074, 95% CI [+0.0131, +0.0494]. Pooling is legitimate only because the roots are shared, so unequal root counts are refused rather than truncated into alignment; and the function hands back the evidence against pooling (max_interaction_z, poolable) so it cannot quietly bury a real interaction. NOTE the CI lower bound +0.0131 is BELOW the 0.03 null band these very claims declared as absent, and this SE prices ROOT noise only — with n=1 training run per arm the dominant term is still unpriced.

t19.claim: The augmenter expresses a 2D board symmetry as a (cell_perm, action_perm) pair, so a game whose action space is not its board width can be symmetry-augmented — tictactoe augmentation no longer throws
t19.note: 2026-09-22, code-forward after the efficiency question closed. augment_examples did x[..., perm] — reindexing the board's WIDTH axis with the action perm — which is correct ONLY when num_actions == board width (Connect-4's columns). tictactoe.symmetries() returned 8 valid 9-cell dihedral perms and augment threw IndexError on the size-3 axis; othello/checkers omitted symmetries() entirely for this reason (documented in test_othello). Now each symmetry is (cell_perm len rows*cols, action_perm len num_actions): the board is flattened and permuted by cell_perm, the policy by action_perm, aux ownership by cell_perm, aux reply by action_perm. Connect-4 is byte-identical (guarded). This UNBLOCKS othello + checkers symmetries (deferred units) but does not add them. neural.py is a TRAINING_MODULE so this MOVES THE ERA off 3f2bacd402c7 — acceptable: no comparison is outstanding, and connect4/othello behaviour is unchanged.

t20.claim: A game's exploitable symmetries are FOUND by proving each candidate isometry commutes with its own dynamics (side-to-move preserved), not hand-asserted — and checkers has the left-right mirror, correcting the hand-guess of identity-only
t20.note: §C.36, 2026-09-22. harness/symmetry.py: dihedral_isometries enumerates the board's shape-preserving isometries; verify_isometry keeps one only if transform(step(s,a))==step(transform(s),action_perm[a]) for every legal a over 200 random positions with current_player preserved (== value-invariance). Games supply two small encoding-aware hooks (transform_state, transform_action); enumeration + verification are generic. Results: connect4 {id,flip_h} (byte-identical to the old hand-written pair), tictactoe full D4=8, checkers {id,flip_h}. The checkers result CORRECTS my own earlier hand-analysis ('likely identity-only'): flip_h flips only the column component so the men's forward direction survives; rot180/flip_v reverse it and the diagonal maps rotate it sideways, all refused BY THE VERIFIER. 6/6 mutations killed incl. each individual check isolated by a fake game that lies one way. games/ + symmetry.py are NOT fingerprinted, so the era stays 1bab977cec75. t21.claim: A change's effect across games is read as ONE verdict with multiplicity counted across the row (N games = N comparisons at alpha/N): generalises only if every game moves the same way, contested if signs disagree, local if only some move, null vs inconclusive split by the null band
t21.note: §C.20/§C.38, 2026-09-22. harness/matrix.py — the cross-game regression matrix the fingerprint was built for (§C.17). Rows=a change, columns=games, cells=a paired delta (from paired_exploitability/paired_conversion via cell_from_compare). The row verdict is DERIVED, in the register's vocabulary: significance at the CORRECTED bar alpha/N, direction from SIGNIFICANT cells only (a non-sig cell abstains, sign '0'), generalises requires ALL games, contested if significant signs disagree, local if some, null if all |diff|<null_below else inconclusive. Caveats travel through per cell (L6). 6/6 mutations killed incl. sign-from-significant-only and the <= boundary; scripts/cross_game_matrix.py drives a real sweep (smoke-run on connect4+tictactoe with the augment lever -> INCONCLUSIVE, correct at 6 openings) or assembles from a ledger. matrix.py + scripts not fingerprinted -> era stays 1bab977cec75.

t22.claim: generalises (a conjunction: every game moved) is an intersection-union test at alpha, NOT Bonferroni alpha/N — the corrected bar is for the union question (did any game move); and null requires the whole CI inside the null band, not a small point estimate
t22.note: §C.20, 2026-09-22, from an adversarial review of the matrix. Original code applied alpha/N to BOTH the union and the conjunction, over-correcting generalises so a real transferable lever (all games p<=0.05 but >alpha/N) read inconclusive — the opposite of the truth on the headline verdict. Fix (Berger min-test / IUT theorem, same reason TOST uses alpha not alpha/2): generalises tests each game at alpha; local/contested keep alpha/N (the union family). Also fixed: null now gated on the CI lying inside the null band (TOST equivalence) not the point estimate (the absence-of-evidence fallacy the module rails against); N==1 reads 'single_game' not 'generalises'. 6/6 mutations killed.

t23.claim: A cross-game matrix cell's unit of replication is the TRAINING RUN, not the opening: a single training draw is never significant and carries a standing caveat; significance comes from a between-seed t-test over per-seed deltas
t23.note: §C.20/§C.19, 2026-09-22, the FATAL review finding: the original sweep measured opening variance for ONE net vs ONE net, re-admitting the single-net confound the matrix exists to kill. Fix: cell_from_seed_deltas takes the per-training-seed paired deltas (measured on a FIXED opening set) and tests their mean with a between-seed t-test (new Student's-t primitives student_t_two_sided_p/t_critical in measurement.py, validated against the t-table). One seed -> p=1.0 + provenance caveat, so it can never claim a net-level effect. Exact sample-t formula (sd ddof=1, SE=sd/sqrt(r), df=r-1) mutation-pinned.

t24.claim: Othello exposes the full verified dihedral group (D4=8): the flank-capture rule is direction-agnostic so every rotation/reflection of a position preserves value, and the PASS action is fixed under every symmetry
t24.note: §C.39, 2026-09-22. The deferred othello hook: transform_state relabels the 64-cell board, transform_action maps a cell to its image and PASS->PASS. find_symmetries verifies all 8 D4 against othello's dynamics (measure, don't assert). This MOVES othello's own era 1bab977cec75->f180acfa235f because games/othello.py folds into its fingerprint AND othello training now augments 8x (was identity-only) — a real, intended behavioural improvement; the shared-module canary training_fingerprint(None)=5b2e23684c22 is unchanged, so no training-path drift. t25.claim: Optimality is measurable as STATE-SPACE COVERAGE: the symmetry-reduced fraction of reachable states where an agent's move is in the solver's optimal set — an optimal agent scores 1.0, a weaker one strictly less, and a per-ply breakdown localizes where it fails
